# LaTeX `\rowcolor` Command

The `\rowcolor` command is used to color entire rows in tables. It requires the **`colortbl`** or **`xcolor`** package (with the `table` option).

## Setup

```latex
\usepackage[table]{xcolor}
```

## Basic Syntax

```latex
\rowcolor{color}
```

Or with optional opacity/model:
```latex
\rowcolor[model]{color-spec}
```

## Basic Example

```latex
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage[table]{xcolor}

\begin{document}

\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|}
\hline
\rowcolor{gray!30}
Header 1 & Header 2 & Header 3 \\
\hline
Row 1 A & Row 1 B & Row 1 C \\
\rowcolor{yellow!20}
Row 2 A & Row 2 B & Row 2 C \\
Row 3 A & Row 3 B & Row 3 C \\
\hline
\end{tabular}

\end{document}
```

## Alternating Row Colors

Use `\rowcolors` (note the **s**) to alternate automatically:

```latex
\rowcolors{2}{blue!10}{white}  % start at row 2, alternate blue and white

\begin{tabular}{lll}
\rowcolor{blue!40}
Name & Age & City \\
Alice & 30 & Paris \\
Bob   & 25 & London \\
Carol & 28 & Tokyo \\
Dave  & 35 & Berlin \\
\end{tabular}
```

Syntax: `\rowcolors{starting-row}{odd-color}{even-color}`

## Using RGB / HTML Colors

```latex
\rowcolor[RGB]{255,200,200}
\rowcolor[HTML]{FFCCCC}
\rowcolor{red!50}        % 50% red mixed with white
```

## Common Issues

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| `\rowcolor` not working | Use `\usepackage[table]{xcolor}` (the `table` option is essential) |
| Cell colors override row | `\cellcolor` takes precedence over `\rowcolor` |
| Vertical lines look broken | Known issue; consider using `booktabs` style without vertical rules |
| `\rowcolor` must appear at start of row | Place it **before** the first cell content |

## Combining with `\cellcolor`

```latex
\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|}
\hline
\rowcolor{gray!20}
A & B & \cellcolor{red!40} C \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
```
